verdicts.note: Mandate exposure, DIVORCE outcome. Identified and off-estimand. Keep visible for instrument validity: it is the same identifying variation arm 2 uses.
No abstract. 'Birth outcomes' in Fertility and Sterility usually means perinatal or multiple-birth, not a population quantity; could be P1, OFF_SAFETY or ROUTE_A12.
Mandate exposure, multiple-birth-rate outcome. Routed by OUTCOME per the scope-freeze rule.
Narrative review of US mandates, not an estimate.
Italy 2022: MAR contributed 3.7% of TFR, 5.9% of first order, 16% among older mothers. Arm 1's estimand exactly.
Projection to COMPLETED cohort fertility rather than a period share.
Czechia; explicitly addresses the quantification methodology.
UK 1991-2018, all ART treatments; separates donor-egg treatments.
NBER. Outcome is utilisation, not births — the first link of arm 2's chain.
Australia. CAUTION for extraction: comparing MAR-conceived to non-MAR-conceived conditions on the treatment, so it cannot answer the population-rate question by itself.
Male-infertility coverage mandates; a distinct mandate margin.
No abstract; TITLE IS DECISIVE. Mandate exposure, timing-of-first-birth outcome.
Political economy of WHY states adopt mandates. Bears on whether mandate timing is exogenous — flag for risk of bias, not for the cell.
No abstract; title decisive. Outcome is health-plan expenditure.
No abstract; title decisive. J. Health Economics 2006 — mandate on FERTILITY. A core arm-2 record and it was NOT in the anchor set.
CONTRACEPTION mandates under the ACA, not infertility. Belongs to A.2 (contraceptive access). Right shape, wrong hypothesis.

2026 microsimulation: MAR is UNLIKELY to compensate for cohort fertility decline. Runs against v5's clause; the sign is not given by the theory and this is included on exactly the same terms as a positive finding.
Late-parenthood trends across low-fertility countries.
Explicitly frames the question as demographic relevance of ART uptake in Europe.
Australia's 2010 Medicare cut — a REDUCTION in public funding. Non-US identified variation and a rare downward margin.
Mandate exposure, infant and child HEALTH outcomes. Wall 2 by outcome.
NEJM 2002, CDC clinic data by mandate state. Outcome likely per-cycle and embryos transferred rather than population births.
Affordability exposure, multiple-birth outcome.
No abstract. Massachusetts mandate, cost of services.
NBER 2007. Utilisation AND outcomes of treatment; full text will decide whether a birth count is reported.
Review of European fertility trends that reviews interventions; whether it quantifies ART's share is not visible.
Czechia, projected live births with and without assisted reproduction.
Habbema-style simulation of IVF's effect on birth rates in western countries. NOTE: this is very likely the work v5 miscited as 'Habbema 2009'.
Serbia. Postponement and age-related infertility; ART's recovery role not visible.
No abstract; title decisive. Almost certainly a later version of W1532475510 — flag for the version-of-record check at extraction.
Mean age at childbearing against fertility rate; no ART channel.

France 2026, PUBLICLY FUNDED elective preservation — the exposure PI call 2 asks about, but the outcome here is profiles and motivations, not births. The elective cell so far is populated by attitude studies.
Denmark and UK; frames ART against population ageing.
French tempo/quantum decomposition.
RePEc preprint of the Bitler & Schmidt 2006 anchor. Version-of-record duplicate — flag.
Mandate exposure, multiple-embryo-transfer outcome — a clinical practice variable. Boundary case between Wall 1 and A.12.
PDR 2025, METHODOLOGICAL: how ART's contribution to fertility rates should be conceptualised and measured. Bears directly on PI call 4 (the demographic-significance denominator).
SMART Collaborative — the US ART surveillance linkage infrastructure.
Demography 2024 microsimulation of delayed first births; whether ART is a modelled channel is not visible in the abstract.
Forecasting chapter on low-fertility countries generally.
Delayed fertility as a driver of decline — A.15's question.
Finnish descriptive register study.
Europe's declining population and ART's contribution; reports cycles per million inhabitants.
Systematic review of TFR determinants generally, not ART-specific.
AGE-BASED eligibility restrictions on ART access and reimbursement against late fertility. A genuine P2 record on the legal-availability margin, which the recon probe found thin.
Population 2017. Postponement's biological cost and ART's offset against completed fertility.
BELIEF side, not behaviour: women 35-43 seeking fertility assessment, their intentions and reasons for postponing.
Australia 2017: 6.7% of births MAR-conceived (4.8% ART + 1.9% ovulation induction). Note the OI split — A.12 found OI drives multiples through a channel eSET does not touch.
Commentary on race/ethnicity disparities in ART utilisation.
Polish. Procreative intentions against biological fecundity constraints — belief side.
Lowest-low fertility in Europe; ART is not the subject.
LABOUR-MARKET incidence of infertility mandates (wages and employment of the mandated group). Same identifying variation as arm 2 — keep visible: it speaks to who actually bears the mandate's cost.
Korea's ART insurance coverage against multiple pregnancies and births. Routed by outcome.
State mandates against health-seeking behaviour for infertility.
Normative social-justice essay on involuntary childlessness.
Russia's 2014 inclusion of IVF in state health insurance — a large non-US access expansion.
Educational participation and later childbearing — A.15's, via C.3.b.
General essay on drivers of global fertility decline.
Socio-economic pathways into childbearing delay in Australia.
Economics of ART from a financing/policy perspective; no birth count.
